items.summary: Recommendation: maintain containment-only execution and drain existing work. Highest-leverage friction is operational throughput, not idea supply: 197 approved proposals lack execution requests, 46 failed-request follow-ups remain open, 29 deployed improvements await measurement, only 1 outcome is proven, and the authoritative candidate list is empty. Prioritize existing repair-or-close, measurement, attribution reconciliation, and security evidence work. Product opportunities to retain as deferred concepts are: canonical proposal-to-request lineage with deduplication; explicit improvement lifecycle and measurement states; queue-capacity and blocker visibility; and a fleet control-plane view linking owner, evidence, risk gate, rollback, and outcome. These would save operator time and improve reliability, adoption, reversibility, and measurability, but current capacity and approval gates do not justify creating new work this cycle. Do not add telemetry, requeue failures, deploy, change schedules, expand monetization, or make financial or causal claims. Preserve unknowns, including conflicting AI-usage totals, aggregate unattributed revenue, unavailable operations/fleet-doctor results, and incomplete security/compliance evidence. Keep the gated product private and route any external permission request only after human-counsel review and owner authorization.
